jerseyRenames.note: Now wearing #7 — wore #88 for the Aug 9, 2026 matches (Keystone and Penn Fusion).

matches.read: Out-attempted 8–12 despite a near-even possession split. The defense faced more shot volume than it produced — the closest thing to a warning sign in either result this stretch.

own.note: GOAL — 1–0. #44 breaks the deadlock, the only goal either team needed a full training block to finish clinically. First shot of a productive night for #44 (3 shots total).
Shot, 2nd period. #44 gets in behind again late — the third chance created down this side, a repeatable pattern worth drilling as a set look.

opp.note: GOAL — 1–1. #23 equalizes. Keystone's most productive attacker — involved in 3 of their 6 shots this match (6’, 23’, 32’).
Shot, 2nd period. #23 tests the back line again right after the restart — the same runner created their first and last look of the match.

matches.read: The most dominant attacking output of the stretch (13 attempts to 7, 4 goals) — but conceding 2 goals from only 5 shots against (29% conversion allowed) shows the chances given up were high quality. A fourth goal in the 61st minute turned the comeback into a rout, but the defensive lapse that let Penn Fusion back to 1–2 at the half is still worth reviewing on film.

own.note: GOAL — 4–2, the final margin. #24 caps the comeback with a fourth goal in the 61st minute — a clean finishing move worth showing the group full-speed.
GOAL — 3–2. #44 completes the comeback nine minutes after equalizing, putting Highland ahead for good — review alongside the 61st-minute fourth goal below for the full finish.
GOAL — 2–2. Down 1–2 at the half, #44 levels it right after the restart and swings the momentum for good.

opp.note: GOAL — 0–1. #54 opens the scoring early — worth reviewing the buildup to see what space was conceded in the first 10 minutes.
GOAL — 1–2. #8 restores the lead just a minute after our equalizer — a quick-transition sucker punch worth flagging for defensive shape after we score.

matches.read: A 1–1 draw that carries Veo's own “REDUCED ACCURACY” flag (camera facing the sun, low-contrast kits) — read the shot/goal counts as directionally right, not exact. Highland out-shot NJ14 Bia 4–0 (5–1 in total attempts) and took the lead in the 41st minute, but NJ14 equalized two minutes later. Despite the shot advantage, Highland held only 39% possession — NJ14 controlled the ball more but mostly in deeper areas (57% of their possession in their own defensive third), while Highland's attacking-third share (40%) far outweighed NJ14's (14%). Neither goal has a jersey number tagged by Veo's AI on this match, a direct consequence of the reduced-accuracy flag.

own.note: GOAL — 1–0. Highland breaks the deadlock in the 41st minute — no jersey number tagged by Veo's AI on this match (reduced-accuracy flag).
Shot, 2nd period. #18 gets a late look after coming on — the last real chance created either way.

opp.note: GOAL — 1–1. NJ14 equalizes just two minutes after going behind — no jersey number tagged (reduced-accuracy flag). Their only shot of the match besides this goal came at 38', so this was a quick response rather than a sustained spell of pressure.
Shot, 1st period. NJ14's only non-goal shot logged all match — came right before their equalizer three minutes later.
